add_block.new_heading: What is on a chefs table menu in Dubai?
new_paragraphs: A chefs table menu in Dubai is a multi-course tasting sequence, usually five to nine courses, built around what is in season and what your guests love. Most menus open with a run of canapés or a raw course, move through fish and a main, and finish with a plated dessert. Because this is chefs table food catering, not a fixed list, the menu is written for you. Mediterranean and modern European are popular, but Arabic, Asian and fusion tables all work beautifully. Wine or a non-alcoholic pairing can be woven in course by course. Dietary tailoring is planned in, not bolted on afterward: vegetarian, vegan and halal courses are built into the sequence, and allergen-aware menus are available on request, subject to confirmation by the assigned culinary partner. You approve every dish before the date, and the chef adjusts portion sizes and richness to the length of the evening you have planned.

add_block.new_heading: Chefs table logistics: space, timing and setup
new_paragraphs: A chefs table needs a little more room than an ordinary dinner — a counter, island or setup table the chef can cook and plate from within sight of your guests. Most Dubai villas, apartments and yacht galleys work, and we confirm power, water and prep space when we scope the booking. The team usually arrives two to three hours before service to set up, and clears everything afterward, so your kitchen is left as it was found. A single chef covers smaller tables; larger groups add a commis and a server. Service typically runs two to three hours across the courses, paced so the conversation stays relaxed. If your venue is tight, your chef can prep off-site and finish and plate in front of guests, so you still get the show without the crowding. We plan all of this before the day so nothing is improvised.
